classification.difficultyReason: Transform numerator and denominator using the same auxiliary angle and identify the tangent quotient.

content.prompt:
Find the value of $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ if
$$\frac{\sqrt3\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x}=R\tan(x-\alpha).$$

answer.short:
$R=1,\quad\alpha=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Express the numerator as $2\sin(x-\frac{\pi}{6})$ and the denominator as $2\cos(x-\frac{\pi}{6})$.
answer.worked:
For a common auxiliary angle, coefficient matching gives
$$\begin{align*}2\cos\alpha&=\sqrt3\\2\sin\alpha&=1\\\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{6},\qquad 0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt3\sin x-\cos x&=2\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\\\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x&=2\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right).\end{align*}$$
Where the original quotient is defined,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sqrt3\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x}&=\frac{2\sin(x-\pi/6)}{2\cos(x-\pi/6)}\\\frac{\sqrt3\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x}&=\tan\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right).\end{align*}$$
Therefore $R=1$ and $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{6}$.
